# RG16 `implausible-amount`: A dealt or minted amount is implausible

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** warn (warn)

`deal`, `vm.deal` or `mint` moves at least 10^30 raw units (or `type(uint256).max`), or, on a fork pinned to a block, at least 10^27 raw units.

## Why it matters

An amount that large is not a balance anyone holds and not a trade anyone does. On a pinned fork it also replaces the balance the block actually had, so the profit is computed against a number the chain did not have. The tool does not read the chain, so it cannot know the real balance at that block; the bounds are fixed and stated here. A mislabeled unit (a wei amount described in a comment as a much smaller token amount) is a plausible literal and is not flagged.

## How to fix it

Use an amount a single actor could hold at the pinned block, and say in the report why that size is representative. Do not `deal` over a fork balance that the test could have transferred from its real holder.

## Fires on

```solidity
vm.createSelectFork(rpc, BLOCK);
deal(address(token), attacker, 1_000_000_000_000e18);
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
vm.createSelectFork(rpc, BLOCK);
vm.prank(WHALE);
token.transfer(attacker, 1_000e18);
```

## How it can be wrong

- A token with very few decimals, or a pointed test of an overflow, where 10^27 raw units is the case under test. Say so in an `allow` comment.
- The bound is not the balance at the pinned block. A deal of 1000 tokens on a fork is under the bound even when that address held 1 token at the block. The rule cannot see the block.
- `approve(..., type(uint256).max)` is not a deal or a mint and is not flagged. An infinite approval is not an infinite balance.

## In Solana tests (Rust and Anchor TypeScript)

Not checked. Solana tests are not checked for implausible lamport or token amounts. Writing a program account's balance is RG06.

## In Move tests (Sui and Aptos)

Not checked. Move tests are not checked for implausible amounts. `mint_for_testing` into the attacker is RG06.

## Silencing it

An `allow` comment in the repo under review does not silence this rule, and neither does a `realism.yaml` or `realism-gate.toml` inside that repo. Policy is an operator file outside the tree (`--declaration`, `--config`). `--trust-inline-allows` is the author switch, for a PoC you wrote and are not gating.

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG16) <why this is not a defect here>
```

The comment is the same in Rust, TypeScript and Move. A comment without a reason is ignored even with `--trust-inline-allows`, and the output says so.
